## About
Archie's Gardenland is a garden center on Z Boaz Pl in Fort Worth. We carry indoor and outdoor plants for all kinds of spaces, along with pottery in every size, from small bud vases to big hanging pots.
If you're not sure what will work in your yard or home, ask one of our garden associates. Some plants are easygoing and some are finicky, and we'd rather help you pick something that will do well where you plan to put it.
Come by to shop or browse for ideas. We're rated 4.7 on Google from 399 reviews, and we're glad to be part of the local gardening community.

## Services
- Indoor and outdoor plants: A wide selection of plants for the house, patio and garden, suited to different growing conditions.
- Pottery: A wide pottery selection with something for everyone.
- Help with your space: Talk with a garden associate about what will do well in your yard or home before you buy.

## FAQ
Q: Can I come in just for ideas?
A: Yes. Come in for inspiration or to plan your area, and ask a garden associate about what will suit your space.

Q: What are your Sunday hours?
A: On Sunday we're open 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

Q: Where are you located?
A: We're at 6700 Z Boaz Pl, Fort Worth, TX 76116.

## What customers say
- "Great little hidden gem in FtWorth.  Vast selection of indoor/outdoor plants for various climates, ask a garden associate for help with your own space. Most were suited for the Texas climate, but some can be very finicky so be cautious of making a purchase that won't survive the space you have available in your garden/home. Pottery selection was very impressive and on point, something for everyone from the smallest bud vases to the largest hanging pots you will see in Texas. Proper "Texas" sized pottery we will call it y'all haha.

I think Archie's is a staple for the gardening community, and I would love to see them have a much more extensive employee outreach group that spoke to people and helped them create the space they are there to fill. Being able to envision your personal garden laid out by an associate would increase ticket prices considerably, while helping those who might not know what can mix, and what wont work.

There were a few areas where the inventory was low, I'm not sure if we came after a rush, if the Texas heat killed a bunch, or if they missed a truck from a supplier. Either way, there was plenty of options to get the job done." (Corey Clendening, 5/5)
- "Is this voted #1 garden center in DFW?? Because it should be. A perfect spot for myself a beginner gardener (plant lover). You can come get inspiration or plan your area. This place is HUGE. I really like the dynamic pricing. Every plant is priced by its growth and not just the same by type. It really helped me decide whether to go big or small. I loved the experience and I will probably only shop here from now on." (Jenslyfe, 5/5)
- "Fort Worth’s answer to North Haven Gardens in Dallas! This is truly the best garden center in Fort Worth, thanks to the staff’s incredible knowledge, thoughtful advice, and genuine assistance. They make gardening feel easy and enjoyable. In my opinion, it’s the Neiman Marcus of garden centers—an exceptional experience from start to finish!" (Richard Daly CTC, 5/5)
- "If you love plants, this place is a dream. Knowledgeable staff, beautiful selection, and such a peaceful environment. It’s hard to leave without bringing something home." (Cortney Caylor, 5/5)
- "I’ve been a loyal customer of Archie’s for about five years and have spent thousands of dollars there. When one of the three 7-gallon wax myrtles I purchased failed, I called and spoke with the manager. He told me there wasn’t a formal warranty but asked me to email photos of the shrubs so he could review the situation. I did exactly that but never received any response.

I wasn’t expecting a refund. Even a simple reply or some advice would have been appreciated. If you’re going to ask a customer to take the time to send photos, the least you can do is respond. Unfortunately, the lack of follow-through and customer service is why I’ll be taking my business elsewhere.

Update:

Archie’s Gardenland did eventually reach out to me by email regarding the 7-gallon wax myrtle that failed after purchase. Although they normally do not have a warranty on plants, I really appreciate that they reviewed the situation and gave me credit for the failed wax myrtle.

I’m grateful they were willing to work with me and make it right. Thank you to Archie’s for the follow-up and customer service." (Family Griffin, 4/5)
